items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear, there is a good layout comment at the top of shapeindex_encode.go, and helpers like readCount are documented. Business logic uses single-letter names (`p := &Polygon{}`, `l := decodeLoopState(d)`, `s := &encodedShape{}`), which caps this item at accept.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: shapeindex_encode.go is 541 lines, which caps this at accept. All per-shape codecs live in that one file instead of next to each type (lax_*.go, loop.go), against the project convention. A new `shapeKind` enum duplicates the existing typeTag mechanism, and there is an extra generic `encodedShape` type.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every length goes through readCount with a bound, allocations are capped by decodeChunk, and IDs, cells and chains are validated. But Decode wraps everything in a catch-all `recover()` ("last line of defense"), which hides panics. Decoded Polygon `hasHoles`/`bound` and loop depth are trusted without consistency checks.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: Encode/Decode are added in a new file. Existing per-shape wire formats, typeTag values and the Shape interface are untouched. The only change to an existing file is the internal pendingAdditionsPos loop bound in shapeindex.go, which does not affect any format.
